scope: Diagnostic-only audit of current visible ColorControl, Background/Gradient, Box shadow, Text shadow and Filters UI in built Chrome MV3. Test fixtures provide host CSS; all extension edits use user-visible buttons, fields, sliders, pointer and keyboard. Native computed style reads verify results.

findings.problem: Escape retains a color edit despite the field tooltip promising gesture cancellation
reproduction: Select #checkout in the built-Chrome fixture.
Open Typography and focus Text color.
Replace the native white value with #00ff00.
Press Escape while the field is focused.
findings.expected: Escape restores the white color, consistent with the displayed tooltip 'Escape reverts the current gesture.'
findings.actual: Target stays rgb(0, 255, 0); field stays #00ff00. Undo later restores white.
findings.probableRootCause: EditField passes a NumericScrubber tooltip to ColorControl. ColorControl handles Enter but has no Escape/cancelGesture handler.
findings.recommendedFixPhase: Shared color interaction and truthful tooltip behavior

findings.surface: ColorControl alpha on a valid CSS token
findings.problem: Changing currentColor alpha silently changes its hue to black
reproduction: Select the white-text #checkout fixture.
Open Box shadow and Add box shadow.
Set Box shadow color to currentColor and press Enter.
Open Box shadow color picker and type 50% in Alpha.
findings.expected: Either preserve the rendered white hue while changing opacity, or disable alpha for a token that cannot be resolved safely.
findings.actual: White currentColor shadow becomes rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5); main field is #00000080. Undo restores currentColor.
findings.probableRootCause: The numeric alpha handler calls rgb(parsed ?? '#000') when Culori cannot parse currentColor, replacing a valid unresolved token with black.
findings.recommendedFixPhase: Shared color token handling; disable alpha for unresolved valid tokens until conversion is safe

findings.problem: A valid interpolation hint is displayed as a color stop with an invented position
reproduction: Select #complex-gradient, authored with linear-gradient(90deg, red 0% 20%, 45%, blue 100%).
Open Background and select Layer 1.
Inspect the stop rows and track.
findings.expected: Recognize the standalone 45% interpolation hint as a hint, or preserve the complex syntax in a clearly limited editor instead of displaying it as a CSS color.
findings.actual: Chrome normalizes red 0% 20% into two red stops. UI shows four color rows; Stop 3 color contains invalid color token 45%, with a default position around 66.7%. Native gradient remains valid; angle edit/Undo/Reset preserve its actual CSS.
findings.probableRootCause: parseGradient treats every remaining argument as a color stop. A lone percentage cannot be distinguished as an interpolation hint and receives an implicit-stop editor.
findings.recommendedFixPhase: Rich gradient parser/state presentation; block unsupported hint editing until faithfully represented

findings.surface: Border color for nonuniform four-side colors
findings.problem: Four valid side colors appear as a single unparseable color token with a black/default picker
reproduction: Select #nonuniform, authored with red/green/blue/yellow side colors.
Open Border.
Open Border color picker without editing.
findings.expected: Display a clear mixed/per-side state and explain that choosing one color replaces all sides.
findings.actual: Main field contains the four-value rgb shorthand, swatch appears unset, picker defaults to black and says 'Enter a color, or choose a new one to replace this token.' Applying one color and Undo work correctly.
findings.probableRootCause: A border-color shorthand containing four valid colors is passed into a parser that expects one CSS color.

findings.problem: Invalid popup format input omits aria-invalid although CSS is rejected
reproduction: Open a text/background/border/box-shadow/text-shadow/gradient-stop color picker.
Choose HEX, RGB or HSL.
Replace its formatted text with an invalid color.
findings.expected: Focused invalid format input exposes aria-invalid=true and an associated error.
findings.actual: CSS remains unchanged and visible error appears, but formatted popup input aria-invalid is null. Closed input exposes aria-invalid=true. Confirmed across all six current control contexts.
findings.probableRootCause: The popup formatted input lacks aria-invalid; only the closed color input receives it.

findings.surface: Color controls across Typography and Effects
findings.problem: The same color picker has inconsistent format tabs, swatch shape and input typography across sections
reproduction: Open Text color picker in Typography and select HSL.
Open Box shadow color picker and select HSL.
Compare selected tabs, closed swatches, captions and fields.
findings.expected: Shared color controls follow consistent visual conventions unless the surface difference has a clear user purpose.
findings.actual: Typography uses underline tabs, square swatch, larger code-styled closed field and a divided heading; Effects uses filled segmented tabs, circular swatch and smaller UI-font closed field.
findings.probableRootCause: Typography-only ColorControl CSS overrides deliberately diverge from the shared base color UI.
findings.recommendedFixPhase: Later UI consistency pass; no functional redesign during this audit

sharedRootFindings.problem: Target label/outline render above extension inspector and popover at 320px, including on the color spectrum and shadow color row.
sharedRootFindings.probableRootCause: Selected overlay is in the browser top layer and the inspector/popovers are in normal DOM stacking.

limitations.actual: Current UI exposes 8 fixed-unit numeric controls/ranges (blur px, hue deg, remaining percent). It has Reset but no opacity/drop-shadow editor, individual enable/disable or reorder controls. These absent controls are not unwired visible surfaces.

Repeated blur functions disable the Blur numeric/range controls with the tooltip explaining preservation. New supported filters append without corrupting repeated blur/drop-shadow; Reset and Undo restore the chain. Disabled Blur displays neutral 0px rather than a single merged blur value.

expectedExclusions.category: H. Expected browser/CSS behavior — NOT a bug
expectedExclusions.actual: Chrome resolves authored relative shadow lengths/currentColor to pixel/RGB computed values. Editing y preserves the other computed components and inset; no change is made merely by opening the UI.

expectedExclusions.category: H. Expected browser/CSS behavior — NOT a bug
expectedExclusions.actual: Chrome omits default ellipse and normalizes left top to 0% 0% in radial-gradient, right bottom background-position to 100% 100%, and double-position red to two equivalent red stops. Those normalized values are correct.

expectedExclusions.category: H. Expected browser/CSS behavior — NOT a bug
expectedExclusions.actual: px-to-em shadow conversions yield -3.00001px due to decimal serialization, preserving rendered offset within normal tolerance. Alpha ArrowRight at the maximum is a boundary no-op; the final spec uses ArrowLeft for that case.

coverageStatus: Complete: all five effects Chrome diagnostic groups passed in the final 24-group run; no recorded page errors. Known product defects remain documented observations.
